sanskrit: vidā divo viṣyann adrim ukthair āyatyā uṣaso arcino guḥ | apāvṛta vrajinīr ut svar gād vi duro mānuṣīr deva āvaḥ ||
english: By hymns he knew how to open heaven, to split the mountain — the radiant Dawns came forth in their procession. He unclosed the folds, the light of heaven went upward; the god opened wide the human doors.

sanskrit: vi sūryo amatiṁ na śriyaṁ sād orvād gavām mātā jānatī gāt | dhanvarṇaso nadyaḥ khādoarṇāḥ sthūṇeva sumitā dṛṁhata dyauḥ ||
english: The Sun spread out his glory like splendour; the mother of the kine, the knowing one, went forth from the broad pasture. The rivers that run through desert sands, teeming with foam, — heaven stands firm, well-measured like a pillar.

sanskrit: asmā ukthāya parvathasya garbho mahīnāṁ januṣe pūrvyāya | vi parvato jihīta sādhata dyaur āvivāsanto dasayanta bhūma ||
english: For this hymn the womb of the mountain, primeval source of great beings, opened wide. The mountain cleft apart; heaven was made ready; those who came forward drained the darkness from the earth.

sanskrit: sūktebhir vo vacobhir devajuṣṭair indrā nv agnī avase huvadhyai | ukthebhir hi ṣmā kavayaḥ suyajñā āvivāsanto maruto yajanti ||
english: With well-uttered hymns, with god-pleasing words, I now call upon Indra and Agni for aid. For with hymns do the wise, skilled in sacrifice, adore and worship, making the Maruts draw near.

sanskrit: eto nv adya sudhyo bhavāma pra ducchunā minavāmā varīyaḥ | āre dveṣāṁsi sanutar dadhāmā yāma prāñco yajamānam accha ||
english: Come now, let us today be of clear mind; let us drive away adversity more fully. We place hostilities far in the distance; let us press forward, facing the sacrificer.

sanskrit: etā dhiyaṁ kṛṇavāmā sakhāyo 'pa yā mātāṁ ṛṇuta vrajaṁ goḥ | yayā manur viśiśipraṁ jigāya yayā vaṇig vaṅkur āpā purīṣam ||
english: Let us, O friends, fashion this prayer by which the mother's cow-pen is opened. By which Manu won the wide-flung prize; by which the shrewd trader gained his treasure.

sanskrit: anūnod atra hastayato adrir ārcan yena daśa māso navagvāḥ | ṛtaṁ yatī saramā gā avindad viśvāni satyāṅgirāś cakāra ||
english: Here the stone, set moving by the arms of those who sang, resounded, by which the Navagvas for ten months did praise. Saramā, following the truth, found the cattle; Aṅgiras accomplished all things truly.

sanskrit: viśve asyā vyuṣi māhināyāḥ saṁ yad gobhir aṅgiraso navanta | utsa āsām parame sadhastha ṛtasya pathā saramā vidad gāḥ ||
english: All [the gods] rejoiced with the cattle at the shining of that mighty dawn when the Aṅgirasas exulted. The spring of those [cows] is in the highest abode; on the path of truth Saramā found the cattle.

sanskrit: ā sūryo yātu saptāśvaḥ kṣetraṁ yad asyorvi yā dīrghayāthe | raghuḥ śyenaḥ patayad andho acchā yuvā kavir dīdayad goṣu gacchan ||
english: Let the Sun, drawn by seven horses, come to the field as it extends both wide and long. Swift as a falcon he wings to the soma-press; the young, wise god shines brightly as he goes among the kine.

sanskrit: ā sūryo aruhac chukram arṇo 'yukta yad dharito vītapṛṣṭhāḥ | udnā na nāvam anayanta dhīrā āśṛṇvatīr āpo arvāg atiṣṭhan ||
english: The Sun mounted the bright ocean; he yoked those tawny mares with light-coloured backs. The wise ones guided him as if a boat through water; the hearkening waters stood below.

sanskrit: dhiyaṁ vo apsu dadhiṣe svarṣāṁ yayātaran daśa māso navagvāḥ | ayā dhiyā syāma devagopā ayā dhiyā tuturyāmāty aṁhaḥ ||
english: I set the sun-winning prayer in the waters, by which the Navagvas crossed over in ten months. By this prayer may we be guarded by the gods; by this prayer may we pass beyond all trouble.

sanskrit: hayo na vidvāṁ ayuji svayaṁ dhuri tāṁ vahāmi prataraṇīm avasyuvam | nāsyā vaśmi vimucaṁ nāvṛtam punar vidvān pathaḥ puraetha ṛju neṣati ||
english: Like a knowing horse I have yoked myself to the yoke; I carry this forward-bearing prayer, seeking help. I desire neither to unyoke from it nor to turn back again; the wise one who goes before leads us straight on the path.

sanskrit: agna indra varuṇa mitra devāḥ śardhaḥ pra yanta mārutota viṣṇo | ubhā nāsatyā rudro adha gnāḥ pūṣā bhagaḥ sarasvatī juṣanta ||
english: Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, O gods — let the host of the Maruts advance, and Viṣṇu too; both Nāsatyas, Rudra, and the divine wives; Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Sarasvatī — may they be pleased.

sanskrit: indrāgnī mitrāvaruṇāditiṁ svaḥ pṛthivīṁ dyām marutaḥ parvatāṁ apaḥ | huve viṣṇum pūṣaṇam brahmaṇas patim bhagaṁ nu śaṁsaṁ savitāram ūtaye ||
english: Indrāgnī, Mitrāvaruṇā, Aditi, heaven, earth, sky, the Maruts, mountains, and waters — I invoke Viṣṇu, Pūṣan, the Lord of Prayer (Bṛhaspati), Bhaga, and glorious Savitṛ for aid.

sanskrit: uta no viṣṇur uta vāto asridho draviṇodā uta somo mayas karat | uta ṛbhava uta rāye no aśvinota tvaṣṭota vibhvānu maṁsate ||
english: May Viṣṇu too bring us bliss, and the unwearying Wind; may Soma the wealth-giver create well-being for us. May the Ṛbhus approve our wealth, and the Aśvins; may Tvaṣṭṛ and Vibhu think kindly of us.

sanskrit: uta tyan no mārutaṁ śardha ā gamad divikṣayaṁ yajatam barhir āsade | bṛhaspatiḥ śarma pūṣota no yamad varūthyaṁ varuṇo mitro aryamā ||
english: And may that host of Maruts dwelling in heaven, the adorable ones, come to sit upon our sacred grass. May Bṛhaspati, Pūṣan grant us shelter; may Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman bestow protection.

sanskrit: uta tye naḥ parvatāsaḥ suśastayaḥ sudītayo nadyas trāmaṇe bhuvan | bhago vibhaktā śavasāvasā gamad uruvyacā aditiḥ śrotu me havam ||
english: And may those mountains, so richly praised, bright-shining, and those rivers, be for our protection. May Bhaga, the apportioner, come with strength to aid us; may wide-spreading Aditi hear my call.

sanskrit: devānām patnīr uśatīr avantu naḥ prāvantu nas tujaye vājasātaye | yāḥ pārthivāso yā apām api vrate tā no devīḥ suhavāḥ śarma yacchata ||
english: May the eager wives of the gods favour us; may they promote us toward swift motion and the winning of spoil. Those who dwell on earth, and those who abide in the realm of waters — may those goddesses, easy to invoke, grant us shelter.

sanskrit: uta gnā vyantu devāpatnīr indrāṇy agnāyy aśvinī rāṭ | ā rodasī varuṇānī śṛṇotu vyantu devīr ya ṛtur janīnām ||
english: And may the divine wives advance — Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, the queen Aśvinī. Let Varuṇānī hear and let Rodasī come; may the goddesses advance who are appointed as the season of women.

sanskrit: prayuñjatī diva eti bruvāṇā mahī mātā duhitur bodhayantī | āvivāsantī yuvatir manīṣā pitṛbhya ā sadane johuvānā ||
english: Harnessing [her steeds], the great mother comes from heaven declaring her message, awakening her daughter. The youthful one, full of wisdom, calling repeatedly to the fathers in their abode, seeking to serve them.

sanskrit: ajirāsas tadapa īyamānā ātasthivāṁso amṛtasya nābhim | anantāsa uravo viśvataḥ sīm pari dyāvāpṛthivī yanti panthāḥ ||
english: Swift they come, flowing in that direction, having mounted the navel of immortality. Boundless and broad, the paths go round them on all sides — heaven and earth encompass them.

sanskrit: ukṣā samudro aruṣaḥ suparṇaḥ pūrvasya yonim pitur ā viveśa | madhye divo nihitaḥ pṛśnir aśmā vi cakrame rajas pāty antau ||
english: The bull, the ocean, the ruddy one, fair-winged, entered the womb of the ancient father. Set in the middle of heaven, the dappled stone strides apart, guarding the two ends of the atmosphere.

sanskrit: catvāra īm bibhrati kṣemayanto daśa garbhaṁ carase dhāpayante | tridhātavaḥ paramā asya gāvo divaś caranti pari sadyo antān ||
english: Four carry him, sustaining welfare; ten nourish the embryo for his moving. The three-fold cows of his highest dwelling range immediately about the bounds of heaven.

sanskrit: idaṁ vapur nivacanaṁ janāsaś caranti yan nadyas tasthur āpaḥ | dve yad īm bibhṛto mātur anye iheha jāte yamyā sabandhū ||
english: This form is the subject of discourse among people: the rivers move where the waters have stood still. When two that are alien to each other sustain the one who has a mother, the twin siblings, born here and there, are kindred.

sanskrit: vi tanvate dhiyo asmā apāṁsi vastrā putrāya mātaro vayanti | upaprakṣe vṛṣaṇo modamānā divas pathā vadhvo yanty accha ||
english: The waters extend their powers for him; the mothers weave garments for the son. The bulls, rejoicing beside the watering-place, go along the paths of heaven toward the bride.

sanskrit: tad astu mitrāvaruṇā tad agne śaṁ yor asmabhyam idam astu śastam | aśīmahi gādham uta pratiṣṭhāṁ namo dive bṛhate sādanāya ||
english: May that be so, O Mitrāvaruṇā; may that, O Agni, be declared auspicious and healing for us. May we obtain firm ground and a firm footing; adoration to the great heaven, the abiding-place.

sanskrit: kad u priyāya dhāmne manāmahe svakṣatrāya svayaśase mahe vayam | āmenyasya rajaso yad abhrā āṁ apo vṛṇānā vitanoti māyinī ||
english: For what dear abode shall we now direct our thought — that realm of its own sovereignty and its own glory, great and mighty? — When the magic one, gathering the clouds, spreads out the waters of that raw sky.

sanskrit: tā atnata vayunaṁ vīravakṣaṇaṁ samānyā vṛtayā viśvam ā rajaḥ | apo apācīr aparā apejate pra pūrvābhis tirate devayur janaḥ ||
english: They spread out a course that swells with heroes; with a common flowing they embrace the entire atmosphere. The waters retreat to the west and farther; the god-devoted man crosses over by means of the former [paths].

sanskrit: ā grāvabhir ahanyebhir aktubhir variṣṭhaṁ vajram ā jiharti māyini | śataṁ vā yasya pracaran sve dame saṁvartayanto vi ca vartayann ahā ||
english: With the pressing-stones, with the ever-recurring days and nights, the magic one drives forward the mightiest bolt. A hundred or more move about in its own house, revolving the days and turning them apart again.

sanskrit: tām asya rītim paraśor iva praty anīkam akhyam bhuje asya varpasaḥ | sacā yadi pitumantam iva kṣayaṁ ratnaṁ dadhāti bharahūtaye viśe ||
english: I have seen the flood of it as an axe facing forward, its marvellous form. When, together, it places a treasure like a nourishing dwelling for the folk at the invocation of Bhara.

sanskrit: sa jihvayā caturanīka ṛñjate cāru vasāno varuṇo yatann arim | na tasya vidma puruṣatvatā vayaṁ yato bhagaḥ savitā dāti vāryam ||
english: He, four-faced, strains forward with his tongue, Varuṇa, handsomely arrayed, pressing against the foe. We do not know him in his human measure, from whom Bhaga and Savitṛ bestow the desirable gift.

sanskrit: devaṁ vo adya savitāram eṣe bhagaṁ ca ratnaṁ vibhajantam āyoḥ | ā vāṁ narā purubhujā vavṛtyāṁ dive-dive cid aśvinā sakhīyan ||
english: I seek for you today divine Savitṛ and Bhaga, who distributes the treasure of life. O ye two lords, many-nourishing Aśvins, I would turn you toward us as friends day after day.

sanskrit: prati prayāṇam asurasya vidvān sūktair devaṁ savitāraṁ duvasya | upa bruvīta namasā vijānañ jyeṣṭhaṁ ca ratnaṁ vibhajantam āyoḥ ||
english: Knowing the course of the mighty one, honouring divine Savitṛ with well-spoken hymns, the worshipper should draw near with homage, recognising him as he distributes the foremost treasure of life.

sanskrit: adatrayā dayate vāryāṇi pūṣā bhago aditir vasta usraḥ | indro viṣṇur varuṇo mitro agnir ahāni bhadrā janayanta dasmāḥ ||
english: Without giving, he distributes the desirable things; Pūṣan, Bhaga, and Aditi clothe themselves in radiance at dawn. Indra, Viṣṇu, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni — those wondrous ones generate the auspicious days.

sanskrit: tan no anarvā savitā varūthaṁ tat sindhava iṣayanto anu gman | upa yad voce adhvarasya hotā rāyaḥ syāma patayo vājaratnāḥ ||
english: May resistless Savitṛ grant us that protection; may the rivers, flowing freely, follow that course. When the hotr of the sacrifice has uttered this, may we be lords of wealth, possessing prize and treasure.

sanskrit: pra ye vasubhya īvad ā namo dur ye mitre varuṇe sūktavācaḥ | avaity abhvaṁ kṛṇutā varīyo divaspṛthivyor avasā madema ||
english: Those who direct homage to the Vasus as much as they should, who utter fair words to Mitra and Varuṇa — may the terrible [enemy] retreat; create greater space; with the aid of heaven and earth may we rejoice.

sanskrit: viśvo devasya netur marto vurīta sakhyam | viśvo rāya iṣudhyati dyumnaṁ vṛṇīta puṣyase ||
english: Every mortal should choose the friendship of the divine leader. Every one desires wealth; let him choose the glory that he may thrive.

sanskrit: te te deva netar ye cemāṁ anuśase | te rāyā te hy āpṛce sacemahi sacathyaiḥ ||
english: Those, O divine leader, who obey this command of thine — them, together with their wealth, with them and their attainments, may we truly associate.

sanskrit: ato na ā nṝn atithīn ataḥ patnīr daśasyata | āre viśvam patheṣṭhāṁ dviṣo yuyotu yūyuviḥ ||
english: From there, honour our men, our guests; from there, honour our wives. May the quick one drive far away all obstacles that stand in the path.

sanskrit: yatra vahnir abhihito dudravad droṇyaḥ paśuḥ | nṛmaṇā vīrapastyo 'rṇā dhīreva sanitā ||
english: Where the carrier [Agni], harnessed, has rushed into the trough like a beast, with manly mind, dwelling with heroes, he will win the streams like a wise man.

sanskrit: eṣa te deva netā rathaspatīḥ śaṁ rayiḥ | śaṁ rāye śaṁ svastaya iṣaḥstuto manāmahe devastuto manāmahe ||
english: This, thy lord of the chariot, O divine leader, brings bliss and wealth — bliss for wealth, bliss for well-being. Praised by the Iṣas we offer prayer; praised by the gods we offer prayer.

sanskrit: agne sutasya pītaye viśvair ūmebhir ā gahi | devebhir havyadātaye ||
english: Come, O Agni, with all thy aids, to drink the pressed soma; come with all the gods to receive the offering of oblations.

sanskrit: ṛtadhītaya ā gata satyadharmāṇo adhvaram | agneḥ pibata jihvayā ||
english: Come, you who meditate on sacred order, whose laws are true — come to the sacrifice. Drink with the tongue of Agni.

sanskrit: viprebhir vipra santya prātaryāvabhir ā gahi | devebhiḥ somapītaye ||
english: Come, O sage among the inspired, with the inspired sages, with those who go forth at dawn; come with the gods to drink the soma.

sanskrit: ayaṁ somaś camū suto amatre pari ṣicyate | priya indrāya vāyave ||
english: This soma, pressed in the bowls, is poured into the vessel — dear to Indra, dear to Vāyu.

sanskrit: vāyav ā yāhi vītaye juṣāṇo havyadātaye | pibā sutasyāndhasas abhi prayaḥ ||
english: Come hither, Vāyu, for the feast, pleased with the gift of oblations; drink of the pressed plant — gladly forward to the joy.

sanskrit: indraś ca vāyav eṣāṁ sutānām pītim arhathaḥ | tāñ juṣethām arepasāv abhi prayaḥ ||
english: Both Indra and Vāyu are worthy to drink these pressed [soma drinks]; let the two of you, sinless ones, take pleasure in them — forward to the joy.

sanskrit: sutā indrāya vāyave somāso dadhyāśiraḥ | nimnaṁ na yanti sindhavo abhi prayaḥ ||
english: The soma draughts mingled with curds are pressed for Indra and for Vāyu; they flow like rivers to the low ground — forward to the joy.

sanskrit: sajūr viśvebhir devebhir aśvibhyām uṣasā sajūḥ | ā yāhy agne atrivat sute raṇa ||
english: In accord with all the gods, in accord with the Aśvins and with the Dawn — come, O Agni, as Atri [came], and rejoice in the pressed soma.

sanskrit: sajūr mitrāvaruṇābhyāṁ sajūḥ somena viṣṇunā | ā yāhy agne atrivat sute raṇa ||
english: In accord with Mitrāvaruṇā, in accord with Soma and Viṣṇu — come, O Agni, as Atri [came], and rejoice in the pressed soma.

sanskrit: sajūr ādityair vasubhiḥ sajūr indreṇa vāyunā | ā yāhy agne atrivat sute raṇa ||
english: In accord with the Ādityas and the Vasus, in accord with Indra and Vāyu — come, O Agni, as Atri [came], and rejoice in the pressed soma.

sanskrit: svasti no mimītām aśvinā bhagaḥ svasti devy aditir anarvaṇaḥ | svasti pūṣā asuro dadhātu naḥ svasti dyāvāpṛthivī sucetunā ||
english: May the Aśvins measure out well-being to us, and Bhaga; may divine, resistless Aditi grant well-being. May Pūṣan the mighty establish well-being for us; may heaven and earth with good guidance grant well-being.

sanskrit: svastaye vāyum upa bravāmahai somaṁ svasti bhuvanas yas patiḥ | bṛhaspatiṁ sarvagaṇaṁ svastaye svastaya ādityāso bhavantu naḥ ||
english: For well-being we invoke Vāyu, and Soma, lord of the world, for well-being. Bṛhaspati, with all his host, for well-being — may the Ādityas be for us well-being.

sanskrit: viśve devā no adyā svastaye vaiśvānaro vasur agniḥ svastaye | devā avantu ṛbhavaḥ svastaye svasti no rudraḥ pātu aṁhasaḥ ||
english: May all the Viśvedevas be for our well-being today; may Vaiśvānara, good Agni, be for our well-being. May the god-like Ṛbhus protect us — for well-being; may Rudra guard us from distress — for well-being.

sanskrit: svasti mitrāvaruṇā svasti pathye revati | svasti na indraś cāgniś ca svasti no adite kṛdhi ||
english: Well-being through Mitrāvaruṇā, well-being through the prosperous road. May Indra and Agni grant us well-being; make well-being for us, O Aditi.

sanskrit: svasti panthām anu carema sūryācandramasāv iva | punar dadadāghnatā jānatā saṁ gamemahi ||
english: May we walk along the path of well-being like the sun and moon. May we come together again with those who give again, who do not slay, who know.

sanskrit: pra śyāvāśva dhṛṣṇuyārcā marudbhir ṛkvabhiḥ | ye adrogham anuṣvadhaṁ śravo madanti yajñiyāḥ ||
english: Praise boldly, O Śyāvāśva, with bold hymns, with the singer Maruts — those adorable ones who, free from guile and true to their nature, rejoice in glory.

sanskrit: te hi sthirasya śavasaḥ sakhāyaḥ santi dhṛṣṇuyā | te yāmann ā dhṛṣadvinaś tmanā pānti śaśvataḥ ||
english: For they are friends of steady strength, bold in their going. In their course, self-moving and bold, they protect without ceasing.

sanskrit: te syandrāso nokṣaṇo ati ṣkandanti śarvarīḥ | marutām adhā maho divi kṣamā ca manmahe ||
english: They, swift-running and untiring, leap through the nights. Of the Maruts indeed we think in their greatness in heaven and on earth.

sanskrit: marutsu vo dadhīmahi stomaṁ yajñaṁ ca dhṛṣṇuyā | viśve ye mānuṣā yugā pānti martyaṁ riṣaḥ ||
english: In the Maruts we place our praise and sacrifice, boldly — they who through all ages of mankind guard the mortal from harm.

sanskrit: arhanto ye sudānavo naro asāmiśavasaḥ | pra yajñaṁ yajñiyebhyo divo arcā marudbhyaḥ ||
english: Deserving are they, bountiful givers, heroes of unbounded strength. Offer the sacrifice to the sacrifice-worthy ones — sing forth to the Maruts from heaven.

sanskrit: ā rukmair ā yudhā nara ṛṣvā ṛṣṭīr asṛkṣata | anv enāṁ aha vidyuto maruto jajjhatīr iva bhānur arta tmanā divaḥ ||
english: With their ornaments of gold, with their weapons, the tall heroes let fly their spears. The lightnings followed them, the Maruts like crackling fires; the light of heaven shone of itself.

sanskrit: ye vāvṛdhanta pārthivā ya urāv antariṣa ā | vṛjane vā nadīnāṁ sadhasthe vā maho divaḥ ||
english: They who have grown great on earth, or in the wide atmosphere, whether in the meeting-place of rivers, or in the great abode of heaven.

sanskrit: śardho mārutam uc chamsa satyaśavasam ṛbhvasam | uta sma te śubhe naraḥ pra syandrā yujata tmanā ||
english: Praise aloud the Marut host, of true might, of skilful power. And then those bright heroes harness the swift [steeds] of themselves for their splendour.

sanskrit: uta sma te paruṣṇyām ūrṇā vasata śundhyavaḥ | uta pavyā rathānām adrim bhindanty ojasā ||
english: And the pure ones dwell wrapped in wool upon the Paruṣṇī; and with the wheel-rims of their chariots they cleave the rock with power.

sanskrit: āpathayo vipathayo antaspathā anupathāḥ | etebhir mahyaṁ nāmabhir yajñaṁ viṣṭāra ohate ||
english: Those that go on the path, those that go astray from the path, those that go within the path, those that go along the path — by these names the sacrifice spreads itself out and is accomplished for me.

sanskrit: adhā naro ny ohate adhā niyuta ohate | adhā pārāvatā iti citrā rūpāṇi darśyā ||
english: Then the heroes carry it off; then the Niyuts carry it off. Then [they are called] 'those from afar' — marvellous their visible forms.

sanskrit: chandaḥstubhaḥ kubhanyava utsam ā kīriṇo nṛtuḥ || te me ke cin na tāyava ūmā āsan dṛśi tviṣe ||
english: The praisers, the kubha-dwellers, who utter chants, danced to the spring. Those of them that were like thieves were to me as helpers in the flash of sight.

sanskrit: ya ṛṣvā ṛṣṭividyutaḥ kavayaḥ santi vedhasaḥ | tam ṛṣe mārutaṁ gaṇaṁ namasyā ramayā girā ||
english: Those tall ones, lightning-speared, who are wise and creative — that Marut troop, O Ṛṣi, honour with soothing song.

sanskrit: accha ṛṣe mārutaṁ gaṇaṁ dānā mitraṁ na yoṣaṇā | divo vā dhṛṣṇava ojasā stutā dhībhir iṣaṇyata ||
english: Toward the Marut troop, O Ṛṣi, [go] with gifts like a friend and a woman; praised with inspired thoughts, may the bold ones of heaven be impelled with power.

sanskrit: nū manvāna eṣāṁ devāṁ acchā na vakṣaṇā | dānā saceta sūribhir yāmaśrutebhir añjibhiḥ ||
english: Now, thinking of these gods, let me go to them as to a stream-bed. Let the gifts accompany the generous patrons, those heard on their course, bright and adorned.

sanskrit: pra ye me bandhveṣe gāṁ vocanta sūraya pṛśniṁ vocanta mātaram | adhā pitaram iṣmiṇaṁ rudraṁ vocanta śikvasaḥ ||
english: Those patrons who spoke of the dappled cow as mine, as my kin, who called her their mother — the knowing ones then spoke of the mighty Rudra as father.

sanskrit: sapta me sapta śākina ekam-ekā śatā daduḥ | yamunāyām adhi śrutam ud rādho gavyam mṛje ni rādho aśvyam mṛje ||
english: Seven and seven, the mighty ones each gave me hundreds. On the Yamunā, glorious beyond measure — I groom away the wealth in cattle; I groom away the wealth in horses.

sanskrit: ko veda jānam eṣāṁ ko vā purā sumneṣv āsa marutām | yad yuyujre kilāsyaḥ ||
english: Who knows the birth of these? Who was formerly in the favour of the Maruts when these bays were yoked?

sanskrit: aitān ratheṣu tasthuṣaḥ kaḥ śuśrāva kathā yayuḥ | kasmai sasruḥ sudāse anv āpaya iḷābhir vṛṣṭayaḥ saha ||
english: Who has heard of those who stood in the chariots, how they set out? Toward whom did they flow to Sudās, following him with refreshment — the rains together with libations?

sanskrit: te ma āhur ya āyayur upa dyubhir vibhir made | naro maryā arepasa imān paśyann iti ṣṭuhi ||
english: Those heroes who come with the bright heavenly [lights], rejoicing, blameless young men — they said to me: 'Behold these; praise them thus!'

sanskrit: ye añjiṣu ye vāśīṣu svabhānavaḥ srakṣu rukmeṣu khādiṣu | śrāyā ratheṣu dhanvasu ||
english: They who shine with their ointments, with their axes — self-luminous in their garlands, golden ornaments, and arm-rings — gleaming also in chariots and bows.

sanskrit: yuṣmākaṁ smā rathāṁ anu mude dadhe maruto jīradānavaḥ | vṛṣṭī dyāvo yatīr iva ||
english: Following your chariots, O Maruts, swift givers, I have placed my delight; the rains of heaven [come] like those who hasten.

sanskrit: ā yaṁ naraḥ sudānavo dadāśuṣe divaḥ kośam acucyavuḥ | vi parjanyaṁ sṛjanti rodasī anu dhanvanā yanti vṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: The bountiful heroes shook for the pious devotee the treasury of heaven; they release Parjanya; the rains go along the two worlds in their course across the desert.

sanskrit: tatṛdānāḥ sindhavaḥ kṣodasā rajaḥ pra sasrur dhenavo yathā | syannā aśvā ivādhvano vimocene vi yad vartanta enyaḥ ||
english: The rivers, cleaving a way through the dust with their rush, flow forward like milch cows. Like wet horses released from their road when the steeds swing onward.

sanskrit: ā yāta maruto diva āntarikṣād amād uta | māva sthāta parāvataḥ ||
english: Come hither, O Maruts, from heaven, from the atmosphere, from the near and from the far. Do not stand aloof from us in the distance.

sanskrit: mā vo rasānitabhā kubhā krumur mā vaḥ sindhur ni rīramat | mā vaḥ pari ṣṭhāt sarayuḥ purīṣiṇy asme it sumnam astu vaḥ ||
english: May neither Rasā, nor Kubhā, nor Krumu detain you; may not Sindhu hold you; may not the Sarayu with its flood-tide stand in your way. May your favour rest with us.

sanskrit: taṁ vaḥ śardhaṁ rathānāṁ tveṣaṁ gaṇam mārutaṁ navyasīnām | anu pra yanti vṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: That fierce host of yours, O Maruts, that troop of chariots of the newer ones — the rains follow in their wake.

sanskrit: śardhaṁ-śardhaṁ va eṣāṁ vrātaṁ-vrātaṁ gaṇaṁ-gaṇaṁ suśastibhiḥ | anu krāmema dhītibhiḥ ||
english: Band by band of theirs, troop by troop, company by company with fair praises — may we follow them with our devotions.

sanskrit: kasmā adya sujātāya rātahavyāya pra yayuḥ | enā yāmena marutaḥ ||
english: For whom today have the Maruts gone forth on this course — to the nobly-born one, to him whose sacrificial gift is bestowed?

sanskrit: yena tokāya tanayāya dhānyam bījaṁ vahadhve akṣitam | asmabhyaṁ tad dhattana yad va īmahe rādho viśvāyu saubhagam ||
english: The imperishable grain-seed that you carry for offspring and progeny — bestow that upon us: the wealth and all-sustaining good fortune that we seek from you.

sanskrit: atīyāma nidas tiraḥ svastibhir hitvāvadyam arātīḥ | vṛṣṭvī śaṁ yor āpa usri bheṣajaṁ syāma marutaḥ saha ||
english: May we pass through slanders, cross over them with well-being, casting away blame and enemies. Having rained down the healing remedy at dawn for well-being, may we be, O Maruts, in your company.

sanskrit: sudevaḥ samahāsati suvīro naro marutaḥ sa martyaḥ | yaṁ trāyadhve syāma te ||
english: Rich in gods, abounding in heroes is that mortal man, O Maruts, whom you protect. May we be such.

sanskrit: stuhi bhojān stuvato asya yāmani raṇan gāvo na yavase | yataḥ pūrvāṁ iva sakhīṁr anu hvaya girā gṛṇīhi kāminaḥ ||
english: Praise the bountiful ones — in the going of the one who praises thus, the cattle resound like [cattle] in the pasture. From where you call the former friends: summon the willing ones with your voice, praise them!

sanskrit: pra śardhāya mārutāya svabhānava imāṁ vācam anajā parvatacyute | gharmastuhe diva ā pṛṣṭhayajvane dyumnaśravase mahi nṛmṇam arcata ||
english: Forth to the Marut host, self-luminous, mountain-shaking — I sent forth this utterance; sing great heroic glory to those who praise the heat, who sacrifice on the back of heaven, who are renowned in splendour.

sanskrit: pra vo marutas taviṣā udanyavo vayovṛdho aśvayujaḥ parijrayaḥ | saṁ vidyutā dadhati vāśati tritaḥ svaranti āpo vanā parijrayaḥ ||
english: Forth for you, O mighty, watery, strength-increasing, horse-harnessing, all-running Maruts! Together with lightning they [the waters] pour; Trita cries out; the waters roar in the forests, running everywhere.

sanskrit: vidyunmahaso naro aśmadidyavo vātatviṣo marutaḥ parvatacyutāḥ | abdayā cin muhur ā hrādunīvṛtaḥ stanayandamā rabhasā udojasaḥ ||
english: The heroes great with lightning, stone-hurling, wind-glittering Maruts, mountain-shaking — though again and again veiled by the rain-cloud, roaring and crashing, fierce, water-powerful.

sanskrit: vy aktūn rudrā vy ahāni śikvaso vy antariṣaṁ vi rajāṁsi dhūtayaḥ | vi yad ajrāṁ ajatha nāva īṁ yathā vi durgāṇi maruto nāha riṣyatha ||
english: The Rudras pierce through the nights, the skilful ones through the days, through the atmosphere, through the realms of light — the shakers. When you drove through the plains like ships, through difficulties, O Maruts, you are not harmed at all.

sanskrit: tad vīryaṁ vo maruto mahitvanaṁ dīrghaṁ tatāna sūryo na yojanam | etā na yāme agṛbhītaśociṣo anaśvadāṁ yan ny ayātanā girim ||
english: That heroic greatness of yours, O Maruts, has stretched out long like the Sun's yoke-path. In this your course, you of the unrestrained flame — you came down upon the mountain that gives no horses.

sanskrit: abhrāji śardho maruto yad arṇasam moṣathā vṛkṣaṁ kapaneva vedhasaḥ | adha smā no aramatim sajoṣasaś cakṣur iva yantam anu neṣathā sugam ||
english: Cloud-gleaming host of Maruts, when you plunder the ocean, shaking the tree like a woodpecker, O wise ones — then, together in harmony, lead us, as an eye leads one who moves, on the easy path.

sanskrit: na sa jīyate maruto na hanyate na sredhati na vyathate na riṣyati | nāsya rāya upa dasyanti notaya ṛṣiṁ vā yaṁ rājānaṁ vā suṣūdatha ||
english: He is not conquered, O Maruts, nor slain, nor does he err, nor is he shaken, nor harmed. His wealth does not dwindle, nor his aid — the sage or the king whom you have cherished well.

sanskrit: niyutvanto grāmajito yathā naro aryamaṇo na marutaḥ kabandhiṇaḥ | pinvanty utsaṁ yad ināso asvaran vy undanti pṛthivīm madhvo andhasā ||
english: Bearing the Niyuts, conquering villages like heroes, like Aryaman, O Maruts, trunk-bodied ones — they swell the spring when the mighty ones cry out; they flood the earth with the sweet plant-juice.

sanskrit: pravatvatīyam pṛthivī marudbhyaḥ pravatvatī dyaur bhavati prayaḥbhyaḥ | pravatvatīḥ pathyā antarikṣyāḥ pravatvatantaḥ parvatā jīradānavaḥ ||
english: This earth inclines downward toward the Maruts; heaven inclines downward to those who press forward. The pathways of the atmosphere incline downward; the mountains incline, swift givers that they are.

sanskrit: yan marutaḥ sabharasaḥ svarṇaraḥ sūrya udite madathā divo naraḥ | na vo aśvāḥ śrathayantāha sisrataḥ sadyo asyādhvanaḥ pāram aśnutha ||
english: When you rejoice, O Maruts, full of sound, of solar lustre, at the rising of the sun, O heroes of heaven — your horses never slacken their course; immediately you reach the farther end of this road.

sanskrit: aṁseṣu va ṛṣṭayaḥ patsu khādayo vakṣaḥsu rukmā maruto rathe śubhaḥ | agnibhrājaso vidyuto gabhastyoḥ śiprāḥ śīrṣasu vitatā hiraṇyayīḥ ||
english: Spears on your shoulders, arm-rings on your feet, golden breastplates, O Maruts, gleaming on the chariot; fire-bright lightnings at your wrists; golden helmets spread over your heads.

sanskrit: taṁ nākam aryo agṛbhītaśociṣaṁ ruśat pippalam maruto vi dhūnutha | sam acyanta vṛjanātitviṣanta yat svaranti ghoṣaṁ vitataṁ ṛtāyavaḥ ||
english: That heavenly vault, O nobly-born Maruts, you of the unrestrained flame shake — the bright pippala tree. The righteous ones gathered together, outshining the folds, when they sounded forth their spread-wide cry.

sanskrit: yuṣmādattasya maruto vicetaso rāyaḥ syāma rathyo vayasvataḥ | na yo yucchati tiṣyo yathā divo asme rāranta marutaḥ sahasriṇam ||
english: Of wealth given by you, O all-knowing Maruts, may we be possessors — wealth abounding in chariots and vigour, that does not fail like Tiṣya from the sky. O Maruts, bestow thousandfold upon us.

sanskrit: yūyaṁ rayim marutaḥ spārhavīraṁ yūyam ṛṣim avatha sāmavipram | yūyam arvantam bharatāya vājaṁ yūyaṁ dhatttha rājānaṁ śruṣṭimantam ||
english: You, O Maruts, grant wealth rich in heroes; you protect the sage inspired with sacred song. You assign the swift horse and the prize to Bharata; you set in place the king who hearkens to command.

sanskrit: tad vo yāmi draviṇaṁ sadyaūtayo yenā svar ṇa tatanāma nṝṁr abhi | idaṁ su me maruto haryatā vaco yasya tarema tarasā śataṁ himāḥ ||
english: That wealth I seek from you, O Maruts, instantly helpful — by which we might spread the sun's light for heroes. May this my cherished word find favour with you, O Maruts — by its power may we cross over a hundred winters.
